newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia offers Japan nuclear fuel, gets containers.
newsitem.headline: Russia offers Japan nuclear fuel, gets containers.

text.p: Russia's atomic energy minister said on Monday he would propose selling Japan nuclear fuel during an official visit to Tokyo, Itar-Tass news agency said.

Viktor Mikhailov told Tass in an interview in the Japanese capital that Russia was particularly interested in a commercial contract to supply fuel and also, in particular, to offer services for the enrichment of uranium.

Japan plans to supply Russia with tens of thousands of special containers for the storage of weapons-grade plutonium being removed from the dismantled missiles as part of Russia's decommissioning programme under international arms treaties.

Mikhailov said the containers would be built to Russian specifications at a cost of $2,000 to $5,000 each to hold plutonium at decommissioning sites at Chelyabinsk's Mayak plant, Tomsk-7 and Krasnoyarsk-26.
Japan, he said, was interested in taking part in the construction of a 40,000-container storage dump at Mayak.
